description: Sewer-ML is a sewer pipe defect classification dataset published by the Visual Analysis and Perception (VAP) Lab at Aalborg University with the CVPR 2021 paper by Haurum and Moeslund. It contains 1,300,201 images taken from 75,618 CCTV inspection videos collected by three Danish water utilities over nine years. Every video was annotated by licensed sewer inspectors following the Danish inspection standard Fotomanualen, giving 17 defect classes; images carry multi-label annotations derived by heuristic rules, with training (1,040,129), validation (130,046) and test (130,026) splits and a near 50-50 balance between normal and defective images. Coverage is Danish sewer networks; resolution is the single inspection frame. Format and access: images and annotation files are requested through a form linked from the project page; code is on Bitbucket and trained models on sciencedata.dk. Licence: not stated on the project page. Free. Caveats: access requires a request form, class frequencies are left unbalanced on purpose, and the annotations are extracted from video reports, not drawn per image. Simulation uses: training and benchmarking automated sewer condition assessment, which feeds deterioration and failure models of wastewater networks. Related records: the VideoPipe QV-Pipe and CCTV-Pipe sewer inspection video datasets and the model for automated detection of in-pipe defects in CCTV sewer surveys.
